channel.title: Nik Cubrilovic
channel.description: Writing on security, privacy, and the intersection of technology and society

item.title: Craig Wright is not Satoshi Nakamoto
item.description: An investigation into Craig Wright's claims to be Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto, examining forged evidence and failed cryptographic proofs

item.title: Securing Blockchain.info Users with Tor and SSL
item.description: Helping Blockchain.info become the second site after Facebook to offer a Tor hidden service with a CA-signed SSL certificate, protecting users from MITM attacks

item.title: FBI seizes fake Tor hosted Jihad funding website as part of Operation Onymous, leaves up real site
item.description: During Operation Onymous the FBI seized a fake clone of a jihad funding site while leaving the real version online, highlighting the scattershot nature of the takedowns

item.title: Large Number of Tor Hidden Sites Seized by the FBI in Operation Onymous were Clone or Scam Sites
item.description: The FBI announced the seizure of a large number of darkweb sites to much fanfare. It turns out most of what they got were fake clone sites

item.title: 60 Minutes Australia on Silk Road and Bitcoin
item.description: A breakdown of 60 Minutes Australia's story on Silk Road and Bitcoin, including their confusion between the Deepweb and Darknet concepts

item.title: Analyzing the FBI’s Explanation of How They Located Silk Road
item.description: A technical analysis of the FBI's claims about how they located Silk Road's server, showing their explanation doesn't match how Tor hidden services work

item.title: Notes on the Celebrity Data Theft
item.description: An in-depth look at the underground networks behind "The Fappening" - how they operate, the techniques used to compromise iCloud accounts, and Apple's security weaknesses

item.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Disqus WordPress Plugin
item.description: Disclosure and fixes for a number of bugs in the Wordpress plugin for the popular Disqus commenting system

item.title: CS-Cart v4.2.0 Session Hijacking and Other Vulnerabilities
item.description: How weak session ID generation using uniqid() in CS-Cart allows session hijacking through targeted brute-force, plus a frustrating disclosure timeline

item.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in MyGov, the Australian Government Single-sign-on Solution for Citizen Services.
item.description: Discovering XSS, SQL injection indicators, and poor cookie security in Australia's myGov portal that could expose 2.2 million citizens' tax and health records

item.title: Two Google Chrome Privacy Issues
item.description: Two privacy issues in Chrome where browsing history data persists after deletion - zoom level settings and DNS prefetch data leave traces of visited domains

item.title: Yahoo Axis Chrome Extension Leaks Private Certificate File
item.description: Yahoo shipped their Axis browser extension with the private certificate file used to sign it, allowing attackers to create forged extensions that Chrome trusts

item.title: BlockPlus v4 - Block Google+ widgets and links from other Google sites
item.description: An update to the BlockPlus browser extension which removes Google+ and other sites from the Google homepage and other properties

item.title: Facebook and many other sites also bypass Internet Explorer privacy controls
item.description: Microsoft called out Google for P3P bypass but ignored Facebook doing the same thing - and a survey shows 5% of top sites set invalid P3P headers

item.title: Facebook Is Losing E-Commerce
item.description: Analysis of Facebook's declining e-commerce presence and why users prefer external shopping experiences over Facebook's platform integration

item.title: How Megaupload Was Investigated and Indicted
item.description: A breakdown of the evidence and investigation methods used by the DOJ to indict Megaupload, examining internal emails, financial records, and publicly accessible details

item.title: The Google Firefox search deal, Chrome and Lady GaGa
item.description: Why Google's claim that Chrome is purely altruistic doesn't match their $4.9B marketing spend including Lady Gaga ads and Super Bowl spots

item.title: The Crunchpad is proof of obviousness in the iPad design
item.description: How the CrunchPad tablet project demonstrates the obviousness of the iPad's design, challenging Apple's claims of revolutionary innovation

item.title: The Download Dot-Con
item.description: How CNet's Download.com bundles adware and toolbars with popular open source software, making them no different from the fake download sites they claim to protect against

item.title: Google Android - The Accidental Empire
item.description: How Larry and Sergey purchased Android for $50M without telling Eric Schmidt, and accidentally created a smartphone empire that crushed Nokia and Blackberry

item.title: Introducing Frictionless - Taking the friction out of Facebook social-sharing applications
item.description: Launching Frictionless, a Chrome extension that bypasses Facebook's social reader apps and takes you directly to the original article without sharing your activity

item.title: Lies, Damn Lies and Google+ Statistics
item.description: Debunking the viral "Google+ traffic drops 60%" story based on flawed Chitika statistics with no published methodology - and misunderstanding launch bumps

item.title: Unicode U+F8FF - aka. The Apple Logo Character, on Macs
item.description: The Apple logo character U+F8FF only renders on Mac - on Windows it shows as boxes, Elvish, Tibetan, or embarrassingly as the Windows logo in Wingdings

item.title: Facebook Re-Enables Controversial Tracking Cookie
item.description: Facebook quietly re-enabled the datr tracking cookie on third-party sites after previously removing it, setting cookies on users who never visited Facebook

item.title: How To Setup secure and private Facebook browsing
item.description: Step-by-step guide to securing your Facebook account with two-factor authentication, disabling tracking features, and setting up private browsing

item.title: Facebook Fixes Logout Issue, Explains Cookies
item.description: Follow-up on Facebook's response to the logout cookie tracking issue, detailing the fixes they made and their explanation of how each cookie is used

item.title: Logging out of Facebook is not enough
item.description: When it comes to losing track of Facebook online and preserving your digital privacy - being logged out is far from enough. We find some privacy issues with Facebook and report them.

item.title: Persistent and Unblockable Cookies Using HTTP Headers
item.description: Using HTTP headers as unblockable super-cookies

item.title: BlockPlus - A browser extension to block Google+ notifications
item.description: Releasing BlockPlus, a Chrome extension that removes Google+ links and notifications from the nav bar to prevent the constant distraction of the new social network

item.title: Numeronym
item.description: What i18n and l10n have in common with a16z - the history and rising popularity of numeronyms where letters between first and last are replaced with a count

item.title: Pain and Gain
item.description: The true story of Miami bodybuilders turned amateur criminals using torture as a motivational tool, later adapted into a Michael Bay film

item.title: Finding a Technical Co-Founder
item.description: Advice on finding a technical co-founder including where to network, how to prepare your startup materials, and evaluating technical capabilities

item.title: Guide to Finding a Good and Safe Company or Product Name
item.description: A comprehensive guide to selecting a business or product name, covering domain availability, trademark safety, SEO considerations, and social media presence

item.title: The Google IPO Skeptics
item.description: A look back at the skepticism that surrounded the Google IPO in 2004, when tech industry experts warned investors away from buying shares

item.title: Relevance Time for Twitter
item.description: Why chronological ordering in Twitter is baggage from old computer systems and why relevance-based sorting using user gestures is inevitable

item.title: Fidelio - A browser plugin for secure web browsing
item.description: Releasing Fidelio, a Chrome plugin that defends against Firesheep by forcing HTTPS, rewriting embedded widgets, and setting secure flags on existing cookies
